# ankra_cost_autopilot_override (Resource)

Puts one cluster in a cost autopilot tier whatever its environment kind. Destroying it returns the cluster to its environment's default tier. An override that reaches `expires_at` stops applying and reads as gone, so the next plan recreates it and the platform refuses the past expiry: move `expires_at` forward or remove the resource. The counterpart of `ankra cost autopilot override` and `ankra cost autopilot clear`; it needs `billing.manage` and `clusters.write` on the cluster.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_cost_autopilot_override" "production_freeze" {
  cluster_id = "11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111"
  tier       = "hands-off"
  reason     = "Quarter-end change freeze"
  expires_at = "2027-01-05T00:00:00Z"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Cluster the override applies to. Changing it replaces the override.
- `reason` (String) Why the cluster is overridden, 3 to 500 characters; shown on the cluster's card.
- `tier` (String) Tier: `hands-off`, `scheduled`, `managed` or `ephemeral`.

### Optional

- `expires_at` (String) RFC 3339 instant the override stops applying, in the future. Unset means it never expires.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The cluster id.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Autopilot overrides are imported by cluster id.
terraform import ankra_cost_autopilot_override.production_freeze 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```
